//: Where a fresh install starts, and what the Settings fields accept, written down once for both platforms.
The Mac is the source of truth: NotchBuddy/Sources/App/SettingsDefaults.swift and HomeContent.defaultChoice.

Three checks hold one platform each to this file: tests/SettingsDefaultsTests.swift (the Mac), tests/settings-defaults.ts (DEFAULT_SETTINGS in windows/src/core/state.ts), both run by scripts/test-settings-defaults.sh, and windows/src-tauri/src/settings_defaults_test.rs (Settings::default(), under cargo test).
Keys are the Windows settings fields as settings.json spells them. A key a platform cannot check has to be named as such in that platform's check, with the reason.
platformForced: the defaults Windows keeps different on purpose, each with why. Anything else that differs is a bug on one side.

alwaysVisible.why: A Mac folds the island into a notch that is already black; a PC has no notch, so a folded island is simply gone. Owner decision, 2026-11-20 (docs/parity/README.md).

position.why: The top centre of a Mac screen is the notch; a PC has none, and Windows keeps the island by the clock. Owner decision, 2026-11-20 (docs/parity/README.md).
